newsitem.title: INDIA: India infrastructure needs not properly packaged.
newsitem.headline: India infrastructure needs not properly packaged.

text.p: India's ability to attract foreign capital for infrastructure projects will depend on the proper packaging of these projects, a top Surface Transport Ministry official said on Monday.

"The right format has to be formulated in order to attract savings for road privatisation. No serious attempt has been made to tap capital markets for financing roads and ports," said Yogesh Narain, the seniormost bureacrat in the ministry.
Speaking at a workshop on roads and ports, he said it was necessary to train officials who would deal with private investors, and re-orient them towards taking quick decisions.
If decision-making authorities carried on discussions indefinitely, private investors could not be encouraged to invest, Narain said.

According to a government study, 10 billion rupees are required every year to improve existing roads and develop new ones. But because the investment is not forthcoming, India is losing an equal amount in vehicle operating costs, Narain said.
India also needs 500 billion rupees for upgrading and investment in ports in order to add capacity to match expected demand, the study said.
